$comment: Stage 7 page manifest contract. Normalizes Komga's PageDto array into the canonical page list the reader lays out and caches. Shared by Rust (komga_core::reader::manifest) and Swift (KomgaReader.Manifest).

endpoints.$source: specs/openapi/komga-openapi.yaml, Komga 1.26.3. The image endpoint's zero_based parameter defaults to false, i.e. 1-based; the reader always sends it explicitly so a server-side default change cannot silently shift every page.

rules.canonicalNumber: Array position + 1. The manifest array order IS the reading order; PageDto.number is never trusted for ordering.
rules.requestedNumber: The canonical number, sent to the 1-based image endpoint.
rules.drift: Count of entries whose number != index + 1. Diagnostic only: it never reorders or drops pages, because a server that numbers oddly still returns the pages in reading order.
rules.looksZeroBased: True when the first entry's number is 0. Diagnostic only, same reason.
rules.duplicates: Kept as distinct canonical pages. A book can legitimately contain the same image twice; deduplicating would lose content.
rules.size: Only PageDto.sizeBytes is read (i64). PageDto.size is a display string with rounded 1024-based units, so parsing it would misreport; it is ignored. Unknown size is 0.
rules.cacheAccounting: The authoritative byte count is the on-disk file size after the write, never a manifest guess.
rules.dimensions: Missing or non-positive width/height becomes 0, meaning unknown. Unknown dimensions make a page ineligible for double-page pairing, because a page of unknown aspect cannot be proven to be a spread half.
rules.empty: An empty manifest is a hard error state: pageCount 0, paged false. The reader must not synthesize page 1.
rules.paged: True only for image/* pages. EPUB/PDF/CBZ-of-text report non-image media types and must fall back to the file/progression path instead of the image reader (Stage 6 rule R8: reflowable formats never write read-progress page numbers).
rules.cacheKey: safe_key("{serverId}-{bookId}-p{canonical}") — same sanitizer as cover keys, so one directory and one LRU pool serve both.
rules.cacheExtension: Derived from the RESPONSE Content-Type, not from the manifest mediaType, because the server may transcode (?convert=jpeg) or content-negotiate. The recorded local path in SQLite is the only thing the UI may open; the UI never builds a path or a URL.

cases.name: zero-based-looking-server-response
cases.$comment: If a server ever returns number starting at 0, canonical pages must STILL be 1..N and the image request must still use the 1-based endpoint, so page 1 of the reading order is not skipped.

expect.$driftNote: Both entries disagree with their position: number 0 vs canonical 1, number 1 vs canonical 2.

cases.name: gapped-and-duplicate-numbers
cases.$comment: Real archives produce junk numbering. Ordering and count come from position; nothing is dropped.

cases.name: unknown-dimensions-fall-out-of-pairing
cases.$comment: width/height absent => 0 => unknown. page 2 cannot join a spread, so pairing treats it as a one-page spread and the layout stays correct instead of overlapping.

cases.name: epub-is-reflowable
cases.$comment: An EPUB has no image pages. It must not enter the paged reader and must not write read-progress pages.

cases.name: mixed-image-types-in-one-book
cases.$comment: A single archive can mix png and jpeg. The manifest mediaType is a hint only; the stored extension comes from the response Content-Type.

expect.$note: size is a display string and is NOT parsed; 0 means unknown until the file lands on disk.
